title: First Trust Nasdaq Cybersecurity ETF (CIBR-T) Stock Price and News
summary: This article provides real-time stock price and news for the First Trust Nasdaq Cybersecurity ETF (CIBR-T) listed on the TSX. It includes current market data, historical price movements, and top holdings, along with related market news and analysis.

title: Micron launches automotive-qualified low power DDR5 memory
summary: Micron Technology has introduced the industry's first automotive low-power DDR5 (LPDDR5) DRAM memory, which has been hardware-evaluated to meet the stringent Automotive Safety Integrity Level (ASIL) D. This new memory addresses the critical need for robust functional safety in advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) and autonomous driving, offering increased data access speeds and improved power efficiency. Micron's LPDDR5 is compliant with ISO 26262 standards and includes safety mechanisms to detect and control memory errors, supporting automakers in developing safer vehicles.

title: Broadcom CEO Says Demand Is ‘Real’ as Chip Orders Flood In
summary: Broadcom CEO Hock Tan stated that customers are accelerating semiconductor orders at an unprecedented rate, leading to a demand-supply imbalance. He emphasized that this demand is "real" and customers are beefing up purchases to build buffers and avoid future supply shortages. 90% of the company's 2021 chip supply has already been ordered.

title: Sonos speakers hit the road with new Audi EV partnership
summary: Sonos, a company known for its Wi-Fi-connected speakers, is expanding into the automotive industry through a partnership with Audi. The company's audio hardware will debut in the new Audi Q4 E-Tron electric car, set to be unveiled and go on sale later this year. This move follows a common trend among audio companies to offer their sound systems in vehicles, often as optional upgrades.

title: Ericsson-Powered 5G Unleashes Robot for Airport Inspection
summary: A trial at Hans Christian Anderson airport in Denmark demonstrated a Boston Dynamics Spot robot, connected via TDC NET’s Ericsson-powered 5G network, patrolling perimeter fencing for damage. This initiative, a collaboration between Ericsson, TDC NET, and the Danish Technological Institute, showcased 5G's ability to extend the robot's operational range and facilitate real-time data analysis for security and inspection tasks. The successful trial opens doors for new autonomous use cases for robots in various industries.

title: LG AND DXC LUXOFT LAUNCH JOINT VENTURE ALLUTO
summary: LG Electronics and Luxoft, a DXC Technology Company, announced the launch of Alluto, a joint venture focused on advancing digital, consumer-grade experiences in the automotive industry. Headquartered in Santa Clara, CA, Alluto will commercialize production-ready digital cockpit, in-vehicle infotainment, passenger-seat entertainment, and ride-hailing systems based on the webOS Auto platform. This collaboration aims to provide carmakers with an innovative alternative to enhance future mobility experiences by integrating the webOS ecosystem into vehicles.

title: Ethernet switch performance of Cisco, Huawei, Arista, HPE, Juniper
summary: The article details the Ethernet switch and router market performance of Cisco, Huawei, Arista Networks, HPE, and Juniper Networks in Q4 2020 and the full year 2020, based on an IDC report. It highlights revenue changes and market shares for each vendor and provides overall market growth figures for Ethernet switches and routers.

title: Fidelity Magellan ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (BATS:FMAG)
summary: The Fidelity Magellan ETF (FMAG) is an actively managed, non-transparent ETF that invests in fundamentally selected firms globally, tracking the S&P 500 TR USD index. Launched in February 2021, the fund has assets under management of $266.85 million and a net expense ratio of 0.59%. Its top holdings include major tech companies like NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Amazon.com.

title: The evolution of speed: Moore’s Law still applies to Wi-Fi
summary: This article discusses how Moore's Law, which states that the number of transistors in a computer chip doubles every two years, also applies to the evolution of Wi-Fi speed. Gabriel Desjardins, Director Wireless Connectivity at Broadcom, highlights that Wi-Fi throughput has seen a similar biennial doubling, citing the Samsung Galaxy phone series as an example. The article suggests that Wi-Fi 7, with its 320 MHz channels, is expected to continue this trend of increasing speed.

title: Broadcom manages soaring customer growth with Oracle Cloud
summary: Broadcom successfully transitioned to Oracle Sales, Oracle CPQ, and Oracle DataFox Data Management to handle increased customer volume and a new business model after several major acquisitions. This move enabled them to integrate systems, migrate customer data, automate renewals, and improve sales efficiency within a tight deadline, avoiding the extension of a legacy CRM license. The Oracle solutions provided a unified customer view, reduced IT complexity, and enhanced sales operations, including significant improvements in sales compensation accuracy and staff retention.

title: There are many reasons to add Zscaler stock to your portfolio
summary: Zscaler, Inc. (NASDAQ: ZS) has seen rapid customer expansion and stock price growth due to increased demand for cloud security services, particularly during the pandemic. The company's innovative Zero Trust Exchange security service and advanced solutions position it well in the evolving cloud market, despite high valuation concerns compared to peers. Zscaler's strong financial performance, including solid Q2 2021 results, contributes to its recommendation as a stock to consider.

title: Test Automation for Application Security
summary: This article, part of a four-part series on DevSecOps, focuses on how Cisco integrates security testing into its application development lifecycle using its internal Cloud Automated Validation Engine (CAVE). CAVE performs Dynamic Application Security Testing (DAST), SSL/TLS validation, and host configuration auditing to ensure applications meet industry and Cisco's internal security standards before deployment. The authors share lessons learned from developing CAVE, emphasizing the need for custom rules, good seed files for testing, complementing automation with manual penetration testing, and providing early warnings for non-compliance.

title: Is Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO) A Risky Investment?
summary: Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO) carries a significant amount of debt, totaling US$41.9b in January 2021, though its net debt is US$32.3b after accounting for cash reserves. While the company's debt is 2.7 times its EBITDA and its EBIT covers interest expenses 2.9 times, suggesting it's not problematic, its interest cover is a concern. However, strong cash flow generation and a 37% increase in EBIT over the last year indicate a sensible approach to debt and an improved ability to manage it.

title: Marvell closes on $10 billion Inphi deal, expanding data center and 5G business
summary: Marvell Technology has completed its $10 billion acquisition of Inphi after receiving approval from Chinese regulators, expanding its reach into data centers and 5G network infrastructure. CEO Matt Murphy noted the deal's overwhelmingly positive global customer support. The acquisition will enhance Marvell's growth in key markets such as 5G, cloud, and automotive, and Inphi's former CEO, Dr. Ford Tamer, has joined Marvell's board.

title: What’s Changed: 2021 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Application Performance Monitoring
summary: This article analyzes Gartner's 2021 Magic Quadrant for Application Performance Monitoring, defining APM and highlighting 17 providers. It details the positions of various vendors, including Dynatrace, AppDynamics, New Relic, and Datadog in the Leaders quadrant, and discusses new developments and focuses for Challengers, Visionaries, and Niche Players in the APM market.

title: Time for Samsung's Most Boring Business to Shine
summary: Samsung's memory chip division, a less glamorous but crucial part of its business, is poised for significant growth. As the global leader in DRAM and NAND chips, Samsung is positioned to capitalize on an anticipated surge in demand. The company's management is urged to leverage this super-cycle to boost earnings from its semiconductor operations.

title: KVH发布采用光子集成芯片的高性能IMU，面向自动驾驶应用
summary: KVH Industries推出了P-1750 IMU和P-1725 IMU，完善了其高性能惯性测量单元（IMU）系列，该系列采用专利光子集成芯片（PIC）技术和高性能加速度计。这些IMU旨在为自动驾驶汽车、无人机、AUV、ROV和平台稳定系统等最具挑战性的应用提供卓越的导航能力、环境稳定性和精确度。KVH的PIC技术提高了可靠性，并使其IMU在漂移和噪声性能方面优于价格较低的MEMS IMU。

title: Gartner Says Global Chip Shortage Expected to Persist Until Second Quarter of 2022
summary: Gartner predicts that the global semiconductor shortage will continue through 2021 and begin to normalize by the second quarter of 2022. This shortage is disrupting supply chains, increasing wafer and device prices, and impacting various electronic equipment types. Gartner advises OEMs to extend supply chain visibility, guarantee supply through partnerships or preinvestments, track leading indicators, and diversify their supplier base to mitigate risks.

title: VMware Board Names Raghu Raghuram as CEO
summary: VMware has appointed Rangarajan (Raghu) Raghuram as its new Chief Executive Officer and a member of the Board of Directors, effective June 1, 2021. Raghuram, currently Executive Vice President and Chief Operating Officer, Products and Cloud Services, has been instrumental in shaping VMware's strategic direction since 2003. The company also announced that Sumit Dhawan has been named President, leading all go-to-market functions, and reported preliminary Q1 FY22 results showing an expected revenue increase of 9.5% to $2.994 billion.

title: Putting the Chip Shortage into the Context of Long-Term Trends
summary: The article analyzes the current global semiconductor shortage, attributing it to supply chain rigidities, high barriers to entry, and geopolitical tensions exacerbated by COVID-19. It highlights the long-term trends driving increased semiconductor demand, such as 5G, AI, and electric vehicles, and discusses how governments and companies are responding to secure future supply chains and potentially re-shore manufacturing.

title: SOXX Versus SOXL Semiconductor ETF Forecast: Which Is a Better Buy?
summary: This article compares two semiconductor ETFs, SOXX and SOXL, to determine which might be a better investment. SOXL is a leveraged ETF offering 3x daily returns, leading to higher performance during bull markets but also higher risk. SOXX is a plain ETF for risk-averse, long-term investors, with both ETFs holding similar top companies and having a positive medium-term outlook despite the cyclical nature of the industry.

title: Turbo-charging your Wi-Fi: Aruba launches world’s first enterprise-grade Wi-Fi 6E AP
summary: Aruba, a division of HPE, has launched the world's first enterprise-grade tri-band Wi-Fi 6E-capable access point, the AP-635. This new AP supports up to seven 160 MHz channels in the 6 GHz band, offering an aggregated data rate of 3.9 Gbps, 2.6 times greater than non-6E units. It aims to significantly boost enterprise Wi-Fi connectivity, making 80 MHz channels the new norm and eliminating the need for network redesigns due to overlapping coverage layers.

title: How Nvidia plans to own the data center with AI
summary: Nvidia aims to revolutionize enterprise computing by making data centers run 10 times faster at one-tenth the cost, leveraging its strong position in AI architectures. The company plans to disrupt Intel's x86 dominance through Arm-based architectures, integrated chip designs, and a compelling software consumption model. The article highlights Nvidia's strategic moves, financial standing, and the potential impact of its proposed acquisition of Arm Ltd. on the data center market.

title: J. Bucy Obituary (1928 - 2021)
summary: J. Fred Bucy Jr., former President and CEO of Texas Instruments, passed away on May 20, 2021, at the age of 92. He was a distinguished engineer and leader, known for his significant contributions to electronics and his dedication to Texas Tech University. Bucy's life was marked by professional achievements, including pioneering work in integrated circuits and microprocessors, and a deep personal love for his wife, Odetta, for whom he provided dedicated care during her illness.

title: Here to stay: Implications and opportunities from Taiwan’s semiconductor edge
summary: Taiwan's semiconductor industry dominance stems from decades of government policy and private sector innovation, creating a thriving ecosystem. This leadership is sustained by aggressive R&D investments and high barriers to entry, making it difficult for new competitors to catch up. Structural demand drivers like 5G, AI, and EVs are expected to fuel continued growth in semiconductor sales, presenting attractive opportunities for active investors within Taiwan's broader semiconductor ecosystem.

title: Marvell Extends PAM4 DSP Cloud Data Center Leadership with Industry's First Integrated Solution
summary: Marvell has announced its Atlas 50Gbps PAM4 DSP chipset solution, which integrates transimpedance amplifiers and laser drivers into a single mainstream CMOS technology solution. This advancement significantly reduces power consumption by 25% and simplifies the supply chain for high-performance cloud data centers, computing, and AI applications. The Atlas DSP platform is designed for high-volume markets, offering cost-effective, highly integrated, and reliable technology essential for massive data center growth.

title: La influencia del covid en las 1.000 empresas más grandes de Colombia
summary: The COVID-19 pandemic significantly impacted Colombia's largest companies in 2020, with their combined income falling by 7.6% and profits by 34.1%. Ecopetrol maintained its lead despite a 30% revenue reduction, while D1 entered the top 10 and Avianca saw a dramatic drop. Despite these challenges, the companies demonstrated patrimonial solidity, with assets growing by 2.5% and equity by 0.6%.

title: TSMC considers chip fab in Kumamoto, its first Japanese semiconductor factory
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) is weighing plans to build its first semiconductor factory in Japan, specifically in Kumamoto Prefecture, near a Sony factory. This move, driven by global chip shortages and geopolitical tensions, would involve incentives from the Japanese government and would supply chips to customers like Sony. The potential Japanese plant is part of TSMC's broader global expansion, which includes significant investments in the US, China, and Europe, alongside substantial spending in Taiwan.

title: Nvidia’s takeover of Arm gets support from Broadcom and other chip heavyweights
summary: Broadcom, MediaTek, and Marvell have publicly expressed their support for Nvidia's $40 billion acquisition of Arm, despite scrutiny from antitrust regulators and concerns from rivals like Qualcomm, Google, and Microsoft. These chip heavyweights cite assurances from Nvidia regarding increased investment in Arm's technology and continued fair access for the industry. The support comes as Nvidia and Arm CEOs argue the deal is necessary to meet growing demand and accelerate technological roadmaps in the semiconductor industry amidst a global chip shortage.

title: Cerebras Systems Appoints Rebecca Boyden as General Counsel
summary: Cerebras Systems has appointed Rebecca Boyden as Vice President and General Counsel, leveraging her 20 years of experience with public companies like Broadcom and Avago. Boyden's expertise in business, executive, and legal matters, including managing corporate finance and legal risks during hyper-growth, will be crucial as Cerebras expands internationally and continues its technological innovation. Her appointment comes as Cerebras experiences significant growth, marked by new product launches, international office openings, and prestigious industry recognition.

title: Salesforce Sells $8 Billion of Bonds to Fund Slack Acquisition
summary: Salesforce.com Inc. has completed an $8 billion bond sale to finance its $27.7 billion acquisition of Slack Technologies Inc. The debt offering, which saw more than $32 billion in orders, aims to expand Slack's reach within the corporate employee sector.

title: Ahead of the Apple iPhone 13 Launch, These Chip Makers Look Like Buys
summary: As the launch of Apple's iPhone 13 approaches in September, Barclays analyst Blayne Curtis has identified several mobile-chip makers as promising investment opportunities. Qorvo, Cirrus Logic, Skyworks, and Broadcom are highlighted as favored stocks that could benefit from the anticipated product release. The article suggests that the market sees significant upside not only for Apple but also for its component suppliers.

title: The SoC Evolution: From Early Handsets To Edge Intelligence
summary: System-on-a-Chip (SoC) technology has evolved significantly from early mobile phones to its current role in powering edge intelligence for the Internet of Things (IoT). Initially driven by the need for miniaturization and efficiency in handsets, SoCs now integrate complex functionalities like wireless communication, AI, and machine learning, enabling power savings and local decision-making in IoT devices. This evolution continues to be critical for the growth and advancement of connected technologies.

title: Synthesis and design of filters and multiplexers with acoustic transversal topology
summary: This paper explores the synthesis and design of filters and multiplexers using a novel acoustic transversal topology, detailing its application with both bulk acoustic wave (BAW) and surface acoustic wave (SAW) resonators. It also introduces an approach using coupled resonator filters (CRF) that eliminates the need for a BALUN stage by controlling the phase of each transversal path. The methodology is verified through a fully simulated 9-plexer example.

title: IBM Shuffles Executive Ranks With Departure of President - WSJ
summary: Jim Whitehurst, IBM's second-highest-ranking executive and former Red Hat chief, is departing the company two years after its $33 billion acquisition of Red Hat. Whitehurst, who served as president, will stay on as an adviser. This move comes as big tech firms are heavily investing in data centers for the expanding $214 billion cloud computing market.

title: Gibson Dunn, Latham advise Broadcom on FTC antitrust settlement
summary: Gibson Dunn & Crutcher and Latham & Watkins represented Broadcom Inc. in an antitrust settlement with the Federal Trade Commission. The settlement requires Broadcom to cease demanding customers buy source components exclusively from them, though Broadcom disputed the FTC's characterization of its business. Lawyers involved included Stephen Weissman from Gibson Dunn and Daniel Wall from Latham.

title: Top Semiconductor Companies In India
summary: This article lists the top semiconductor companies in India, highlighting their services and contributions to the industry. It notes that despite a global chip shortage, the Indian semiconductor market is projected to grow significantly, with various companies establishing or expanding their operations in the country to meet demand and leverage local talent.

title: Broadcom in talks to buy software firm SAS Institute - WSJ
summary: Broadcom Inc is reportedly in talks to acquire software firm SAS Institute Inc for a deal valued between $15 billion and $20 billion, according to the Wall Street Journal. This potential acquisition would allow Broadcom to expand its infrastructure software solutions business. SAS Institute provides data and analytics solutions to a wide range of customers globally across various industries.

title: WSJ News Exclusive | Broadcom in Talks to Buy Software Firm SAS
summary: Broadcom Inc. is reportedly in talks to acquire SAS Institute Inc., a move that would further expand the chip maker's presence in the enterprise software market. The potential deal could value the privately held SAS between $15 billion and $20 billion and might be finalized in the coming weeks. This valuation includes assumed debt and adjustments for cash on SAS's balance sheet.

title: Broadcom in talks to buy software firm SAS
summary: Broadcom Inc. is reportedly in talks to acquire SAS Institute Inc., a privately held software firm, for an estimated $15 billion to $20 billion. This potential deal aligns with Broadcom's strategy to expand its enterprise software business, following previous acquisitions like CA Technologies and Symantec's enterprise unit. The move also comes amidst increased scrutiny on large tech mergers from the Biden administration.

title: Will Broadcom's SAS Acquisition Transform Software Industry?
summary: This article discusses the potential acquisition of SAS by Broadcom, examining whether this deal could significantly transform the software industry. It highlights the strategic implications of Broadcom, a semiconductor and infrastructure software company, moving to acquire a major player in analytics software. The piece delves into the possible impact on the market landscape and future technological trends.

title: SAS Institute valuation: Why talks with Broadcom stalled over a possible $15-$20 billion sale
summary: Data analytics firm SAS Institute Inc. has reportedly ended talks with Broadcom Inc. regarding a potential sale valued between $15 billion and $20 billion, due to a change of heart by its co-founders. Jim Goodnight and John Sall, who founded SAS, decided against the sale, possibly influenced by concerns about Broadcom's acquisition strategy and SAS's unique employee-centric culture and high investment in R&D. Despite this setback, analysts believe Broadcom will continue its acquisition pursuit to drive growth.

title: Global software company to acquire SAS, say insiders
summary: Broadcom Inc., an American semiconductor manufacturing company, is reportedly in talks to acquire software company SAS Institute Inc. for an estimated $15 billion to $20 billion. This potential acquisition would further expand Broadcom's infrastructure software solutions business, aligning with its strategy of growing through significant acquisitions. SAS Institute, based in Cary, is a business analytics software developer that recently transitioned to a subscription-based SaaS model.

title: Synaptics Makes a Natural Progression to Edge AI
summary: Synaptics, historically known for interface products, is now heavily investing in edge AI for consumer IoT and computer vision. The company's AI roadmap includes high-end multi-TOPS processors like the VS680 and ultra-low-power solutions like the Katana Edge AI SoC for battery-powered devices. Through strategic acquisitions and partnerships, Synaptics is leveraging its long history in neural networks and pattern recognition to develop advanced on-device deep-learning models addressing privacy, security, and latency concerns.

title: Nvidia Stock’s Surge Makes Chip Maker 10th-Biggest U.S. Listed Company
summary: Nvidia Corp. has become the 10th-largest U.S. public company due to a surge in its stock, driven by the post-pandemic boom in the semiconductor business. The company's shares have increased by nearly 80% over the past year, resulting in a market value of approximately $453 billion. This valuation exceeds the combined market capitalization of its rivals Intel Corp. and Broadcom Inc.

title: ON Semi’s Image Sensors and SiPMs Give AutoX a Leg Up on Autonomous Driving
summary: AutoX, a leader in level-4 autonomous vehicle technology, has secured a license to operate RoboTaxis in China, leveraging ON Semiconductor's image sensors and SiPM technology for 360° vision. The integration includes twenty-eight 8.3 Megapixel image sensors and four LiDAR sensors, significantly enhancing safety and eliminating blind spots in dense urban environments. This partnership highlights the critical role of advanced sensing technology in the advancement of autonomous driving, despite legal and financial hurdles faced by other companies aiming for higher levels of automation.

title: What’s Changed: The 2021 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Privileged Access Management
summary: This article highlights the key changes in the 2021 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Privileged Access Management (PAM), the third iteration of the report. It details how Gartner defines PAM, analyzes the intensely competitive market, and reviews the placements of various vendors within the Niche Players, Challengers, and Leaders quadrants, noting significant shifts for several companies and the absence of new vendors.

title: Japan's 1st commercial-use quantum computer starts operations
summary: Japan has launched its first commercial-use quantum computer, a joint effort between the University of Tokyo and IBM, placing it in a competitive field alongside the U.S. and China. The system, installed in Kanagawa Prefecture, will be used by an industry-academia consortium including companies like Toyota and Sony to explore practical applications and develop human resources in quantum computing. This initiative marks the second IBM Quantum System One built outside the U.S., emphasizing its significance for Japan's research and development in this advanced technological domain.

title: Marvell inks $1.1B deal to acquire network chip startup Innovium
summary: Marvell Technologies Inc. announced a $1.1 billion deal to acquire Innovium Inc., a startup specializing in network processors for cloud data centers. The acquisition will be financed entirely with Marvell shares and is expected to add $150 million to annual revenues by fiscal year 2023. Innovium's chips, known for their efficiency and integration, have rapidly gained market share, securing a contract with a Tier 1 cloud customer that will significantly boost its 2022 revenue.

title: Marvell Tech to acquire Innovium for $1.1 Billion
summary: Marvell Technology is set to acquire networking chip startup Innovium for $1.1 billion to enhance its market share in networking chips for large cloud-computing companies and data centers. The acquisition aims to bolster Marvell's portfolio, particularly with Innovium's Teralynx chips, which compete with Broadcom in the market for data center traffic controllers. This move follows Marvell's previous $10 billion acquisition of Inphi Corp, indicating a strategic effort to expand its cloud business offerings amid significant consolidation in the semiconductor industry.

title: Ecopetrol adquirió las acciones del Ministerio de Hacienda en ISA por $14,2 billones
summary: Ecopetrol announced the acquisition of the Ministry of Finance's 51.4% stake in Interconexión Eléctrica S.A. ESP (ISA) for $14.2 trillion. The transaction, priced at $25,000 per share, solidifies Ecopetrol's position as the majority owner of ISA and is considered a significant step for Colombia's energy sector and transition. Both companies will remain state-owned, with the deal aiming to strengthen strategic goals and attract investment.

title: Open code software giant Elastic to buy Israeli startup, open Tel Aviv R&D site
summary: Elastic NV announced its acquisition of Israeli cybersecurity startup Build.security and the establishment of an R&D site in Tel Aviv. Build.security, founded in January 2020, specializes in authorization policy management for cloud-native environments. This acquisition further expands Elastic's presence in the cybersecurity sector and its operations in Israel.

title: T-shirt fundraiser with Tractor Supply and Carhartt supports skilled trades jobs
summary: Tractor Supply Company and Carhartt have partnered to launch a "Support the Trades" T-shirt fundraiser to help address the skilled trades gap in the U.S. Proceeds from the exclusive T-shirt sales at Tractor Supply will benefit SkillsUSA, a nonprofit dedicated to preparing students for careers in trade, technical, and skilled service occupations. Both companies have committed a maximum donation of $50,000 each, totaling $100,000, to support SkillsUSA's mission to expand its reach and training capabilities.

title: Maxim Integrated Products acquired by Analog Devices to bolster semiconductor production
summary: Analog Devices, Inc. has completed its acquisition of Maxim Integrated Products, Inc. Maxim stockholders received 0.63 of a share of ADI common stock for each share of Maxim common stock, and Maxim common stock will no longer be traded on NASDAQ. Tunç Doluca and Mercedes Johnson, former Maxim board members, have joined the ADI Board of Directors.

title: Vertical Cavity Surface Emitting Laser (VCSEL) Market
summary: Market Insights Reports has published a research report on the Vertical Cavity Surface Emitting Laser (VCSEL) market, highlighting its expected growth over the forecast period (2020-2025) with a CAGR over 18%. The report utilizes primary and secondary research methods, including SWOT and Porter's Five Forces Analysis, and provides an in-depth study of geographic regions, revenue forecasts, segmentation, and market share. A key trend identified is the significant share held by Gallium Arsenide (GaAs) in VCSEL applications, driven by its adoption in 3D sensing in consumer electronics like the iPhone and continuous integration in data communications and gesture recognition.

title: Semiconductor ETF
summary: The VanEck Semiconductor UCITS ETF provides targeted exposure to the semiconductor sector, crucial for the ongoing "fourth industrial revolution" encompassing AI, 5G, and IoT. This ETF, the first of its kind in Europe, invests in pure-play semiconductor companies globally, focusing on those generating at least half their revenue from semiconductors. It highlights the high barriers to entry in the semiconductor industry, which protect profit margins for leading manufacturers.

title: Broadcom forecasts upbeat current-quarter sales on 5G bet
summary: Broadcom Inc. forecasted fourth-quarter revenue above Wall Street expectations, driven by strong demand for semiconductors due to 5G adoption and hybrid work models. The company's wireless division, including Apple as a major customer, is also expected to benefit from new iPhone launches. Broadcom's diversification into software business has helped mitigate supply chain disruptions.

title: Intel CEO Predicts Chips Will Be More Than 20% of Premium Vehicle BOM by 2030
summary: Intel CEO Pat Gelsinger predicts that semiconductors will constitute over 20% of the total premium vehicle bill of materials by 2030, a significant increase from 4% in 2019, driven by "the digitization of everything." To meet this escalating demand, Intel plans to expand chip production in Europe and establish dedicated foundry capacity in Ireland. Additionally, the company's subsidiary Mobileye showcased its production autonomous vehicle and announced plans for a robotaxi service in Germany in 2022.

title: Focal Point Names Scott Pomerantz, formerly of Global Locate and Broadcom, as CEO
summary: Focal Point Positioning, a UK-based deep tech startup, has appointed Scott Pomerantz as its new CEO. Pomerantz, who founded Global Locate and later sold it to Broadcom, brings 30 years of experience in positioning and semiconductors. Focal Point's Supercorrelation technology aims to improve GPS chip performance in various devices, and Pomerantz will lead the company's efforts to scale up technical support, customer integration, and commercialization.

title: Broadcom server-storage connectivity sales down but recovery coming
summary: Broadcom reported an overall increase in revenues and profit for its third fiscal quarter of 2021, despite a nine percent drop in server-storage connectivity sales. The company anticipates a recovery in this segment, driven by enterprise customers, cloud migration to 18TB disk drives, and a transition to next-gen SAS and NVMe products. Broadcom is also accumulating cash, potentially for acquisitions in areas like SmartNICs, as it continues to develop specialized silicon for hyperscalers.

title: VMware Appoints Kit Colbert as Chief Technology Officer
summary: VMware, Inc. announced the appointment of Kit Colbert as its new Chief Technology Officer (CTO). Colbert, who joined VMware in 2003 and has held various key roles including Cloud CTO, will be responsible for shaping the company's technical vision, driving innovation, and overseeing research and development efforts. CEO Raghu Raghuram highlighted Colbert's passion, technological expertise, and leadership as crucial for the company's innovation and R&D advancement.

title: Time-of-Flight 8x8 Multi-Zone Ranging Sensor from STMicroelectronics Enables Innovative Applications
summary: STMicroelectronics has launched the VL53L5CX, its first multi-zone FlightSense™ time-of-flight sensor for general-purpose applications. This sensor offers up to 64 sensing zones, multi-target detection up to four meters per zone, and a broad 63° diagonal field of view, making it suitable for gesture recognition, 3D room mapping in robotics, and various level monitoring applications. The VL53L5CX supports innovative features like motion indication and selectable sensing array resolutions, including an 8x8 zone mode for AR/VR, and is available for immediate order.

title: Roundup: More 6 GHz Wi-Fi in the US, Liberty Global upgrades with Plume, more 6 GHz Wi-Fi in Europe, & latest from Plume IQ
summary: This roundup covers significant advancements in Wi-Fi technology and adoption. The FCC is moving closer to authorizing standard power 6 GHz Wi-Fi in the US, with conditional approvals for AFC systems expected to start after November 30. Liberty Global is upgrading millions of European homes with Plume's intelligent Wi-Fi services, and more European countries are greenlighting 6 GHz Wi-Fi operation. Additionally, Plume IQ reports a growing preference for Smart TVs over streaming STBs and the rising trend of 4K video consumption.

title: Caixin Explains: What’s at Stake in the Massive Unigroup Restructuring
summary: Tsinghua Unigroup Co. Ltd., a Chinese semiconductor giant, is undergoing a massive bankruptcy restructuring to address its significant debts and revive its promising businesses. Several companies, including Alibaba Group and various government-backed enterprises, have expressed interest in bidding for Unigroup's assets, which include its critical chipmaking and cloud computing units. The restructuring aims to find strategic investors with the financial capacity to take over and further invest in key projects like Yangtze Memory Technologies, crucial for China's semiconductor independence.

title: Shares of this obscure chip component supplier have surged by over 1200% in the past three years
summary: Shares of Nan Ya Printed Circuit Board Corp., an obscure Taiwanese company that supplies essential Ajinomoto build-up film (ABF) substrates for chipmaking, have surged over 1200% in the past three years. This surge is due to ABF substrate becoming a critical bottleneck in the semiconductor industry, with supply expected to remain constrained until at least 2025. Major tech companies are struggling to secure enough of this component, leading to increased profits and investment for substrate manufacturers.

title: 5G Technology Devices for an O-RAN Wireless Solution
summary: This article explores the necessary 5G technology devices for successful and cost-effective O-RAN wireless solutions, particularly focusing on the challenges and technological advancements in massive MIMO and small cell deployments. It details Analog Devices' integrated transceiver family, the RadioVerse, and its components like the ADRV9029, ADRF5545A, and DPD functionality, showcasing their role in enabling high-performance, low-cost O-RAN platforms. The author discusses receiver and transmitter signal chain designs, power management, clocking architectures, and the flexibility of these solutions for various 5G applications.

title: The Chip Crunch Grows Worse as Wait Times Hit Record 21 Weeks
summary: The global chip shortage worsened in August, with lead times for semiconductor orders reaching a record 21 weeks. This delay has significantly impacted industries like automotive and electronics, hindering production and growth. While some chip types saw a slight improvement, overall wait times continue to increase.

title: Symantec Endpoint Security: Protection, Prevention and Innovation
summary: This article highlights Symantec Endpoint Security Complete (SESC) as a leading endpoint protection solution, emphasizing its strong performance in independent evaluations like MITRE ATT&CK and Gartner. title: Broadcom launches its lowest power GNSS receiver for mobile, wearables
summary: Broadcom has launched its BCM4778, the lowest power L1/L5 GNSS receiver chip designed for mobile and wearable applications. This third-generation chip is 35% smaller and consumes five times less power than its predecessor, significantly extending battery life. It features advanced multipath mitigation with new Grid Tracking technology, enabling enhanced accuracy and performance for urban navigation.

title: Cover Story: The rise of test equipment giants amid tech boom
summary: The Malaysian semiconductor industry, historically dominated by OSAT companies, is seeing a significant rise in automated test equipment (ATE) manufacturers due to the Fourth Industrial Revolution and AI. title: New Report Highlights Strength of U.S. Semiconductor Industry and Continued Challenges
summary: A new report from the Semiconductor Industry Association (SIA) details the strong global market share and R&D investment of the U.S. semiconductor industry, while also highlighting significant challenges like the ongoing global chip shortage and decreasing domestic manufacturing capacity. The report urges Congress and the White House to fund the CHIPS for America Act and consider an investment tax credit (FABS Act) to enhance U.S. semiconductor production and innovation. These measures are deemed crucial for maintaining America's economic competitiveness, national security, and technological leadership.

title: Digital Turbine Stock, Builders FirstSource, Cricut Among 19 New IBD Watchlist Stocks

title: VMware Charts Course for Customers to Seize Opportunity at the Edge
summary: At VMworld 2021, VMware introduced VMware Edge, a new product portfolio designed to help organizations run, manage, and secure edge-native applications across multiple clouds in both near and far edge locations. The company defines the edge as distributed digital infrastructure close to users and devices, emphasizing the need for a multi-cloud edge to handle emerging workloads like AR/VR and connected vehicles. VMware Edge solutions, including Edge Compute Stack and SASE, aim to provide a consistent and comprehensive approach to edge infrastructure, supported by a broad ecosystem of partners like Dell EMC and Lenovo.

summary: Nvidia has offered concessions to the EU antitrust regulator regarding its $54 billion acquisition of British chip designer Arm. summary: Rambus Inc. has released Compute Express Link (CXL) 2.0 and PCI Express (PCIe) 5.0 controllers that feature integrated Integrity and Data Encryption (IDE) modules. This development, enhanced by the recent acquisition of PLDA, aims to protect against physical attacks on CXL and PCIe links while ensuring data confidentiality, integrity, and replay protection at full 32 GT/s speed.

title: Emerson to Merge Software Units With AspenTech
summary: Emerson Electric plans to merge two of its software businesses, OSI and Geological Simulation Software, with Aspen Technology in an $11 billion cash-and-stock deal. The new combined entity, valued at $160 a share, will retain AspenTech's name and CEO Antonio Pietri. Emerson will contribute $6 billion in cash and own 55% of the new company.

title: EU to investigate Nvidia's $54 bln ARM bid after remedies fall short - sources
summary: The EU is expected to launch an extended antitrust investigation into Nvidia's $54 billion bid for British chip designer ARM. The European Commission is scheduled to end its preliminary review on October 27, initiating a four-month investigation.

summary: Apple is reportedly planning to cut its iPhone 13 production targets for 2021 by up to 10 million units due to ongoing chip shortages impacting key suppliers like Broadcom and Texas Instruments. summary: The article discusses the growing prevalence of IoT devices and the challenge of processing the vast amount of data they generate, especially in the automotive industry. summary: The article discusses how new RF FPGA solutions from Xilinx, specifically the RFSoC and Versal ACAP families, are transforming Electronic Warfare (EW) platforms. title: Renesas’ Innovative Automotive Chips Drive Next-Generation Multimedia System for Toyota Lexus
summary: Renesas Electronics Corporation's R-Car H3 and R-Car M3 system-on-chips (SoCs) have been adopted by Toyota Motor Corporation for their new multimedia systems. summary: GlobalFoundries Inc. made a lackluster Nasdaq debut, with shares opening flat and finishing slightly below its IPO price, valuing the chipmaker at approximately $26 billion. title: Indian American student wins $25,000 top award in science competition
summary: Akilan Sankaran, a 14-year-old Indian American student from New Mexico, won the $25,000 Samueli Foundation Prize in the Broadcom MASTERS competition for his math project on antiprime numbers. Other notable winners included students focusing on wildfire prevention, aquatic drone technology, and obesity research.

title: KLA Corp expands India presence for semiconductor-based R&D
summary: KLA Corporation is expanding its presence in India by opening two new facilities in Chennai to boost semiconductor-based research and talent development. These efforts aim to advance AI, software, image processing, and physics modeling for the global semiconductor industry.

summary: This article discusses how companies like FedEx and S&P Global are adopting cloud edge strategies to move data and applications closer to users, devices, and remote sites. The platform leverages two NVIDIA DRIVE Orin systems-on-a-chip for redundancy and ample compute, supported by a comprehensive sensor suite from leading suppliers like Continental, Hella, Luminar, Sony, and Valeo. Designed to be open and modular, DRIVE Hyperion 8 aims to accelerate the development and deployment of safe and robust autonomous vehicles.

summary: Meta has integrated Cisco and Arista Networks into its Open Compute Project (OCP) efforts by announcing new top-of-rack switches and improvements to its data center fabrics. Meta also shared future goals, including an open die-to-die interface and a commitment to net-zero emissions by 2030.

title: Ex-Broadcom engineer charged in US with stealing secrets for Chinese firm
summary: A former Broadcom engineer, Peter Kisang Kim, has been charged in the US with 18 counts of trade-secret theft for allegedly stealing chip designs for data centers and taking them to a China-based start-up. Kim, who worked at Broadcom for over 20 years, pleaded not guilty and faces a potential 10-year prison sentence for each count if convicted. This case highlights escalated US efforts against Chinese industrial espionage, while also drawing criticism about potential bias against Asian-Americans.

This advancement is crucial for supporting demanding applications like virtual reality, 8K video streaming, and real-time gaming, as well as addressing the growing density of connected devices in homes and enterprises. By providing a "greenfield" spectrum, Wi-Fi 6E minimizes interference and allows for wider channels, ensuring a more robust and efficient wireless experience.

This move complicates an already challenging regulatory path for the acquisition, which has faced opposition from the chip industry and scrutiny from British and European Union regulators. The FTC argues the merger would harm competition, reduce innovation, and lead to higher prices by giving Nvidia the ability and incentive to undermine competitors who rely on Arm's technology.

title: AppNeta Acquired by Broadcom in Order to Bring Its Award-Winning Visibility Platform to the World's Largest Enterprises

Several companies, including Amazon Web Services, Broadcom, Fortinet, HCL, and Okta, have issued advisories and remediation steps for their affected products, warning customers to update or implement temporary mitigations.

title: Wise Road Drops $1.4 Billion Buyout of Magnachip
summary: Chinese private equity firm Wise Road Capital has terminated its $1.4 billion all-cash merger agreement with U.S. chipmaker Magnachip Semiconductor Corp. The termination was due to the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States (CFIUS) failing to approve the deal, citing national security risks. Wise Road Capital will pay Magnachip a $70.2 million termination fee.

summary: Apple is expanding its in-house chip development by hiring engineers for a new office in Irvine, Southern California. Rayala has a strong background in building IT organizations and leading large transformation programs, holding degrees in Chemical Engineering and an MBA.

title: Intel to Buy Israel’s Tower Semiconductor for $5.4 Billion
summary: Intel Corp. has agreed to acquire Israel’s Tower Semiconductor Ltd. for $5.4 billion as part of CEO Pat Gelsinger’s strategy to expand into the outsourced chip-manufacturing business. This acquisition aims to enhance Intel's expertise and customer base in the chip-foundry market, directly competing with industry leaders like Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. The deal is expected to close in about 12 months and is a key part of Intel's broader investment cycle to modernize its factories and rebuild manufacturing capabilities.

title: What’s Changed: 2022 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Enterprise Information Archiving
summary: The article analyzes the 2022 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Enterprise Information Archiving, highlighting the evolving market driven by digital communication and application data. It discusses changes in vendor inclusion criteria, significant movements of key players like Global Relay and Veritas Technologies into the Leaders quadrant, and the strengths of various providers across the Leaders, Visionaries, and Niche Players categories, including Microsoft, Smarsh, Proofpoint, Mimecast, Micro Focus, ZL, Archive360, Solix Technologies, Barracuda, and Jatheon.

title: Ukraine: Disk-wiping Attacks Precede Russian Invasion
summary: Symantec detected a new disk-wiping malware, Trojan.Killdisk, used in attacks against Ukrainian organizations and in Lithuania before Russia's invasion on February 24, 2022. The attacks targeted financial, defense, aviation, and IT sectors, with evidence suggesting preparations began in November 2021. In some instances, ransomware was deployed simultaneously as a decoy to mask the wiper attacks.

title: Intel Boosting Chipmaking With $5.4B Tower Buy
summary: Intel Corp. is set to acquire Tower Semiconductor Ltd. for $5.4 billion to expand its foundry business and meet chip demand. The acquisition aims to leverage Tower's expertise in manufacturing analog chips for various industries and scale Intel's foundry services globally. The deal, pending regulatory approval, is expected to enhance Intel's capacity in the growing foundry market.

title: The role of phase-change memory in automotive OTA firmware upgrades
summary: This article discusses the crucial role of phase-change memory (PCM) in enabling efficient and reliable over-the-air (OTA) firmware upgrades in automotive zone- and domain-based ECU architectures. It explains how PCM addresses challenges like memory cost, update speed, and downtime compared to traditional NOR flash by utilizing a unique dual-cell structure for single-ended mode upgrades, effectively doubling memory capacity during the process. The article highlights PCM's advantages, including faster write operations, no erase requirement, and low power consumption, making it ideal for the next generation of automotive ECUs.

title: GLOBALFOUNDRIES ANNOUNCES NEXT GENERATION IN SILICON PHOTONICS SOLUTIONS AND COLLABORATES WITH INDUSTRY LEADERS TO ADVANCE A NEW ERA OF MORE IN THE DATA CENTER
summary: GlobalFoundries (GF) has announced GF Fotonix™, its next-generation silicon photonics platform, aimed at addressing the explosive growth of data and reducing power consumption in data centers. GF is collaborating with industry leaders including Broadcom, Cisco Systems, Inc., Marvell, and NVIDIA, along with photonic innovators like Ayar Labs and PsiQuantum, to deliver innovative and feature-rich solutions. This monolithic platform, combining advanced photonics features and RF-CMOS on a single silicon wafer, is designed to enable faster, more energy-efficient data transmission and supports various high-growth markets.

title: FIT Introduces QSFP-DD800 Connector / DAC Solutions at OFC 2022
summary: Foxconn Interconnect Technology (FIT) announced that it is jointly exhibiting its QSFP-DD800 interconnection solution with Broadcom and MultiLane at the Optical Networking and Communication Conference & Exhibition (OFC) in San Diego. The solution aims to address the growing demand for higher bandwidth in communication technology (5G/6G) by enabling 800G transmission speeds, crucial for upgrading switch data rates and supporting cloud applications. FIT's QSFP-DD800 also incorporates optimization and immersion cooling technologies to promote lower energy and carbon consumption, assisting partners in achieving carbon neutrality.

title: CAFC Affirms ITC Denial of Broadcom’s Request for Ban on Renesas Products Under Section 337
summary: The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit (CAFC) affirmed the ITC's decision to deny Broadcom's request for a ban on Renesas products. The ITC had denied the ban because Broadcom failed to satisfy the domestic industry requirement under Section 337, as it couldn't demonstrate an actual product protected by its patents. Additionally, the CAFC upheld the Patent Trial and Appeal Board's findings that certain claims of Broadcom's patents were obvious.

title: Here’s How ICE Illegally Obtained Bulk Financial Records from Western Union
summary: Senator Ron Wyden has revealed that Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), a unit within ICE, illegally obtained millions of financial records from Western Union and Maxitransfers Corporation using administrative subpoenas. These subpoenas compelled the companies to provide records of money transfers over $500 to or from certain U.S. states and Mexico, which were then stored in a database accessible to hundreds of law enforcement agencies. This bulk surveillance is deemed illegal due to the misuse of administrative subpoenas, which are statutorily required to seek records "relevant" to specific investigations.

title: Webroot sues CrowdStrike, Sophos, others over alleged patent infringement
summary: Webroot and its parent company OpenText are suing Trend Micro, Sophos, Kaspersky, and CrowdStrike for alleged infringement of several malware detection patents, some dating back to 2005. The lawsuits, filed in the Western District of Texas, claim these defendants infringe upon Webroot's intellectual property related to endpoint security products and platforms. Competitors and observers criticized the move, with CrowdStrike calling it typical of a "patent troll" and others viewing it as "patent bullying."

title: Israel to build high-power laser interceptor
summary: Israeli Defense Minister Benny Gantz has approved a multi-million shekel budget for the development and production of the “Iron Beam” high-power laser system. This system is designed to intercept rockets, mortars, and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), representing a significant technological breakthrough and enhancement to Israel's security capabilities. The project involves the IMOD Directorate of Defense Research and Development (DDR&D), Rafael Advanced Defense Systems Ltd., and Elbit Systems Ltd.

title: Global Navigation Satellite System Market is Projected to Hit USD 320.73 Billion in 2021-2028 | GNSS Industry Exhibit a CAGR of 9.02%
summary: The global navigation satellite system (GNSS) market is projected to grow from USD 175.19 billion in 2021 to USD 320.73 billion in 2028, exhibiting a CAGR of 9.02%. This growth is driven by numerous applications across various sectors and the increasing acceptance of autonomous vehicles. The COVID-19 pandemic has had an affirmative effect on the GNSS market due to boosted supply and demand.

title: Verblecon: Sophisticated New Loader Used in Low-level Attacks
summary: Symantec analysts discovered a new, complex malware loader named Trojan.Verblecon in January 2022, primarily used for installing cryptocurrency miners and potentially stealing Discord tokens. Despite its sophisticated capabilities, the current attacks are low-reward, suggesting the attackers may not fully grasp the malware's potential. If leveraged by more experienced actors, Verblecon could be used for more serious threats like ransomware or espionage campaigns.

title: Global Semiconductor Market to Boost in Coming Years –
summary: The global semiconductor market was valued at USD 550.2 billion in 2021 and is projected to reach USD 820.1 billion by 2028, growing at a CAGR of 5.3%. This growth is primarily driven by the increasing demand for consumer electronic devices and the adoption of advanced technologies like AI and IoT, with the Asia-Pacific region dominating the market. Despite challenges from changing trade policies and high manufacturing costs, the market continues to expand due to surging demand for memory devices and the accelerating pace of digitization.

title: New secure elements authenticate Qi 1.3 wireless charging
summary: Microchip Technology has introduced new secure elements, TrustFLEX ECC608 and Trust Anchor TA100, to authenticate devices using Qi 1.3 wireless charging. These solutions, combined with Microchip's secure key provisioning services, aim to provide an all-in-one secure storage subsystem for consumer and automotive applications, meeting the WPC Qi 1.3 specification's mandate for cryptographic verification of power transmitters. This enables safer and faster wireless charging by authenticating the charger's source and quality.

title: Watkins Represents Broadcom Inc. in US$1.95 Billion Private Senior Notes Offering
summary: Latham & Watkins LLP represented Broadcom Inc. in its US$1.95 billion private senior notes offering. The offering includes US$750 million of 4.00% Senior Notes due 2029 and US$1.2 billion of 4.15% Senior Notes due 2032. The transaction is expected to settle on April 14, 2022.

title: Is QQQ A Good Buy For Dividend Portfolios? Why There Are Better Choices
summary: The Invesco QQQ Trust, Series 1 ETF (QQQ) has seen strong capital appreciation in recent years, largely due to factors like ultra-loose monetary policy and pandemic tailwinds. However, these factors are unlikely to persist, making QQQ less suitable for income-focused dividend portfolios. The author suggests investors might find better income opportunities by selecting individual stocks.

title: KKR to buy cybersecurity firm Barracuda from Thoma Bravo in deal worth about $4 bln
summary: KKR & Co Inc announced its plan to acquire cybersecurity firm Barracuda Networks from Thoma Bravo for approximately $4 billion, including debt. This deal highlights the ongoing strong interest in the cybersecurity sector from buyout firms, fueled by the increase in remote work accelerated by the pandemic and a rise in cyberattacks. Barracuda, founded in 2003, provides cloud-based data security services and generates over $500 million in annual revenue.

title: Broadcom launches Wi-Fi 7 chips
summary: Broadcom has introduced five new Wi-Fi 7 chips designed for residential, enterprise, and mobile applications, aiming to double Wi-Fi bandwidth and improve throughput, latency, and range. A key feature is advanced multi-link operation (MLO), which aggregates channels and rapidly switches between them to optimize data flow in congested networks. This advancement is expected to enhance demanding applications like 16K video streaming, real-time collaboration, and AR/VR, while supporting the growing demand for deterministic wireless data in smart homes and industrial IoT.

title: Lazarus Targets Chemical Sector
summary: The North Korea-linked Lazarus APT group has been observed targeting organizations in the chemical sector in an espionage campaign, a continuation of their "Operation Dream Job." The attacks involve luring victims with fake job offers to install malware. Symantec identified this activity in South Korea, primarily within the chemical sector, noting the use of Trojanized tools and sophisticated lateral movement and persistence techniques.

title: Broadcom Inc. stock falls Thursday, underperforms market
summary: Broadcom Inc. (AVGO) stock fell 3.15% on Thursday, closing at $573.85, a day when the broader market also saw declines. This drop ended a two-day winning streak for the company, leaving its stock $103.91 short of its 52-week high. Competitors such as Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. Ltd. ADR, NVIDIA Corp., and Intel Corp. also experienced declines.

title: Netflix Scores as California Judge Says Broadcom’s Dynamic Resource Provisioning Patent Claim is Abstract under Alice
summary: A U.S. District Judge in California has invalidated a Broadcom patent claim against Netflix, ruling it was an abstract idea under the Alice/Mayo framework. The patent, related to dynamic resource provisioning for job placement, was deemed no different from common task allocation, dealing a setback to Broadcom's patent enforcement campaign against Netflix. This decision is part of ongoing litigation where Broadcom asserts Netflix's streaming services infringe on its server technology patents, affecting Broadcom's traditional set-top box business.

title: Modern Bank Heists 5.0: The Escalation from Dwell to Destruction
summary: The fifth edition of the Modern Bank Heists report reveals a significant escalation in cyber threats targeting financial institutions, moving from "dwell to destruction." Cybercrime cartels are operating like multinational corporations, utilizing dark web economies and state protection to launch destructive attacks, ransomware, and economic espionage. The report emphasizes the need for increased security budgets and proactive measures like extended detection and response (XDR) and regular threat hunting to combat these evolving threats.

title: Nvidia's GPU-powered AI is creating chips with 'better than human design'
summary: Nvidia is leveraging its GPU-powered AI to develop and design new computer chips, including its own GPUs, leading to designs that are "better than human." The company's chief scientist, Bill Dally, explained how AI is used to accelerate chip design processes like power estimation, parasitic prediction, and automated standard cell migration. This approach not only significantly reduces design time and labor but also results in more efficient and smaller chip components, showcasing a win-win scenario for Nvidia's internal development and its AI hardware offerings.

title: Oi ends sale of mobile service, targets fiber
summary: Telecoms company Oi has finalized the sale of its mobile service operation, Oi Móvel, to Telefônica Brasil, TIM S/A, and América Móvil’s Claro Participações, bringing in R$14.47 billion. This move allows Oi to focus on its transformation plan, deleveraging debt, and investing in fiber-optic connectivity and digital services. The transaction, though questioned by competitors and consumer protection groups, was approved by regulators with conditioning measures.

title: Broadcom under Antitrust scrutiny from FTC again - The Information
summary: Semiconductor giant Broadcom Inc. is facing renewed scrutiny from the U.S. Federal Trade Commission (FTC) over alleged exclusive agreements with customers. The FTC is investigating complaints that Broadcom is illegally forcing exclusivity, potentially leveraging supply-chain issues as justification. This comes after previous antitrust settlements with the FTC in 2021 and the European Commission in 2020 regarding similar practices.

title: ModalAI launches new autopilot in VOXL 2
summary: ModalAI has launched VOXL 2, a new autopilot powered by the Qualcomm Flight RB5 5G platform, designed for autonomous drones and robots. This 16-gram autopilot boasts high AI computing power, integrating a PX4 flight controller, an 8-core CPU, and 5G connectivity, and is assembled in the USA. VOXL 2 is a result of the Blue sUAS 2.0 initiative and aims to advance the U.S. drone industry by providing a secure and capable solution, especially for GPS-denied environments and beyond visual line-of-sight operations.

title: Top 10 Tech Stocks by Market Capitalization
summary: This article lists the top 10 tech stocks by market capitalization as of April 2022, providing details on each company's industry, market cap, and annualized returns. It also defines tech stocks, explains their characteristics, and discusses why they present significant investment opportunities, highlighting their innovation and growth potential.

title: Texas Instruments introduces new solid state relays for safer EVs
summary: Texas Instruments (TI) has launched a new portfolio of automotive-qualified solid-state relays designed to enhance the safety of electric vehicles (EVs). These new components, including the TPSI3050-Q1 isolated switch driver and TPSI2140-Q1 isolated switch, aim to provide industry-leading reliability, reduce solution size, and lower bill-of-materials costs for 800-V battery-management systems. The integrated isolation technology in these relays offers faster load disconnection and connection compared to electromechanical relays, improving overall system safety and reliability for high-voltage automotive and industrial applications.

title: Broadcom Vs. Marvell: Better Chipmaker Company To Buy (NASDAQ:AVGO)
summary: This article compares Broadcom (AVGO) and Marvell (MRVL) primarily focusing on their semiconductor businesses. It concludes that Marvell has an edge in ASICs and processor technology, while Broadcom excels in analog business and demonstrates a superior M&A strategy with better revenue contribution and margins. The analysis aims to determine the better chipmaker company to buy.

title: Uber Eats pilots autonomous delivery with Serve Robotics, Motional
summary: Uber Eats is launching two autonomous delivery pilots in Los Angeles with Serve Robotics and Motional. These programs are part of Uber's new product range and aim to explore customer and merchant preferences for autonomous delivery, with plans to scale successful models. The partnership with Serve Robotics, an Uber spinout, focuses on shorter trips, while Motional, mainly known for robotaxis, will handle longer distances.

title: CEO steps in as Progressive slammed for 'woke' hiring practices
summary: Progressive CEO Tricia Griffith defended the company's diversity, equity, and inclusion (DE&I) hiring practices after facing criticism from an activist shareholder at the annual meeting. The shareholder, associated with the Free Enterprise project, questioned the prioritization of "skin color and reproductive organs" over merit. Griffith affirmed that DE&I is crucial for growth and reflecting the diverse customer base.

title: Carousell, L Catterton SPAC Merger Talks End Amid Rout
summary: Carousell Pte, a Singapore-based online classifieds marketplace operator, has ended talks to go public through a merger with blank-check company L Catterton Asia Acquisition Corp. The decision comes amid market volatility, macroeconomic uncertainty, and valuation concerns, making it difficult to arrange a private investment in public equity (PIPE). The special purpose acquisition company (SPAC), backed by L Catterton and minority-owned by LVMH, had been in exclusive talks for a transaction that could have valued the combined entity at $1.5 billion.

title: Coherent optics move toward interoperability
summary: At OFC 2022, the OIF demonstrated significant advancements in optical networking, including interoperable coherent optics from various vendors, 112 Gb/sec electrical links, flexible Ethernet, and co-packaging techniques. These innovations address the increasing demand for higher data rates and improved efficiency in data centers and network infrastructure. Future developments include an 800G coherent optics spec and research into 224 Gb/sec electrical interfaces for 1.2 Tb/sec and 1.6 Tb/sec links.

title: Innovation or Intellectual Scam: Patent Damages and Their Exploited History
summary: The article discusses the high financial stakes and potential for exploitation within the patent law industry, focusing on the Caltech v. Apple and Broadcom case where Apple was relieved of a $1.1 billion patent infringement claim. It examines different interpretations of patent damages, the historical context of patent law, and the role of Patent-Assertion Entities (PAEs). The author also explores proposed reforms to patent law, such as viewing patents as a public regulatory system, to better promote innovation and standardize damage calculations.

title: Broadcom in talks to buy VMware
summary: Chipmaker Broadcom Inc. is reportedly in talks to acquire cloud service provider VMware Inc., according to sources familiar with the matter. This acquisition would further Broadcom's diversification into enterprise software, following previous purchases of CA Technologies and Symantec's security division. VMware's market capitalization was $40.3 billion as of Friday's close, with Michael Dell holding a 40% stake and Silver Lake owning 10%.

title: Broadcom in Talks to Acquire VMware, the Cloud Computing Company (Published 2022)
summary: Broadcom, a semiconductor giant, is reportedly in discussions to acquire VMware, a cloud computing company known for its virtualization software. This potential acquisition would expand Broadcom's presence in cloud computing and continue CEO Hock E. Tan's strategy of diversifying beyond chip companies following a blocked deal with Qualcomm in 2018. Following the news, VMware's stock saw a significant increase, while Broadcom's shares experienced a slight dip.

title: Broadcom reportedly in talks to buy VMware
summary: Broadcom Inc. is reportedly in negotiations to acquire enterprise cloud-computing company VMware Inc. Multiple news outlets, including Bloomberg News, Reuters, the New York Times, and the Wall Street Journal, have reported on these ongoing talks. As of Friday, VMware's market capitalization was approximately $40.3 billion, while Broadcom's was about $222 billion.

title: Chipmaker Broadcom in talks to acquire VMware for $60 billion -sources
summary: Broadcom Inc is reportedly in talks to acquire cloud service provider VMware Inc for $60 billion, a move that would significantly expand Broadcom's enterprise software business. The proposed deal, valued at around $140 per share in cash and stock for VMware, represents a 46% premium to VMware's Friday share price. This acquisition aligns with Broadcom CEO Hock Tan's strategy of diversifying beyond chips into infrastructure software.

title: Broadcom in talks to purchase cloud computing company VMware
summary: Chipmaker Broadcom is reportedly in advanced talks to acquire cloud computing company VMware in a cash-and-stock deal, aiming to further diversify its business into enterprise software. This potential acquisition follows Broadcom's previous purchases of CA Technologies and Symantec's security division. VMware's shares jumped on the news, while Broadcom's saw a slight drop, as details of the deal's value remain undisclosed.

title: Premarket Movers: VMware, Deutsche Bank, EQT Corp
summary: This article highlights several companies making significant premarket moves. VMware (VMW) was up 21.7% and Deutsche Bank (DB) saw a 5.3% increase, while EQT Corp (EQT), ZoomInfo Tech (ZI), and Block (SQ) also posted gains. title: Broadcom Inc in talks to acquire VMware: sources
summary: Broadcom Inc. is reportedly in discussions to acquire cloud-computing company VMware Inc., a deal that would significantly expand the chipmaker's software presence. This potential acquisition aligns with CEO Hock Tan's strategy of diversifying Broadcom through software companies. VMware, valued at around US$40 billion, would provide Broadcom with greater access to the data center market, a critical area for growth.

title: What the Club is watching Thursday — Macy's, Williams-Sonoma buck retail trend with strong reports
summary: Macy's (M) and Williams-Sonoma (WSM) provided strong reports, bucking the recent retail trend. Morgan Stanley upgraded Lululemon (LULU), while Broadcom (AVGO) announced its acquisition of VMware (VMW), signaling confidence in enterprise software valuations.
